unit: The student can welcome a guest, introduce a person, make basic small talk, and politely offer a drink.
objective: Offer traditional beverages to a guest.

title: Warm up
subtitle: Offering a drink
question: When you have guests over, what do you usually offer them to drink?
starters: I usually ask if they'd like...

title: Useful language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and have the student repeat it.
Read the definitions and example sentences.
Ask the check questions to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make a new sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: A clear, natural liquid that we drink.
words.example: I drink a glass of water every morning.
words.check: Do you usually drink water from a glass or a bottle?

words.definition: A popular drink made from dried leaves and hot water.
words.example: Would you like a cup of tea?
words.check: Do you prefer hot tea or iced tea?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: A dark drink that is usually served hot.
words.example: Would you like a cup of coffee?
words.check: Is coffee usually served hot or cold?

words.definition: A sweet drink made from fruit.
words.example: Can I get you a glass of orange juice?
words.check: Is juice usually sweet or salty?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to offer a drink to a guest.

linkers.use: A polite way to offer a drink.
A casual way to offer a drink.
A polite way to offer to get someone a drink.

model:
Host: Hi, welcome! Would you like some tea?
Guest: Oh, yes, please. Thank you.

your_turn.teacher: Pretend I'm a guest in your home. Welcome me and offer me some water, coffee, or juice.
your_turn.student: Hi, welcome! Can I get you some juice?

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine I'm a guest in your home. Welcome me and offer me a drink. You have water, tea, coffee, and juice. Use the sentences below to help you.
student_guide: Welcome! Come on in. Would you like some ___?
Hello! It's great to see you. Do you want some ___?
Welcome to my home. Please, have a seat. Can I get you some ___?

title: Real-world scenario
problem: Your tutor is visiting your home. You need to welcome them and offer them a drink.
mission: Offer them water, tea, coffee, or juice.
The tutor will choose a drink.
start: Tutor: Hello! Thanks for having me over.

title: Wrap-up
recap: Phrases: Would you like...? / Do you want...? / Can I get you...?
Skill: You can politely offer a drink to a guest.
final_task: Use one of today's phrases and a vocabulary word to offer your tutor a drink.
challenge: Next time you have a guest, try offering them a drink in English!
